title.narrative: Integrated Area Based Emergency Lifesaving Support and Recovery for Displacement Affected IDP, Host and Returnees in May Tsebri town, Laelay Tselemti/Dima and Tselemti/West Telemt.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project aims to address urgent humanitarian needs in Mai Tseberi, East Tselemti, and West Tselemti woredas, areas severely impacted by conflict, displacement, and limited access to essential services. NRC will implement an integrated, area-based intervention targeting 11,069 direct beneficiaries, including 3,457 women, 2,627 men, and 4,985 children among Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), returnees, and host communities. lt/pgtltpgtThe key sectors of focus are Agriculture, Protection - Housing, Land, and Property (HLP), and Education in Emergencies (EiE).ltbrgtIn the Agriculture sector, NRC will reach 2,551 (1786 female) beneficiaries through the provision of essential agricultural inputs, such as improved seeds, fertilizers, tools, and livestock packages for vulnerable female-headed households. Training on climate-smart practices, sustainable crop management, and income-generating opportunities will empower communities to rebuild resilient livelihoods. lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtProtection interventions will target 1920 (960 female) individuals by addressing Housing, Land, and Property (HLP) issues through legal counseling, rights-awareness sessions, and support for customary dispute resolution mechanisms, thereby fostering social cohesion and reducing land-related tensions.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe EiE component will support 6598 (4,317 children, including children with disabilities) individuals, by providing flexible learning opportunities, psychosocial support, and child protection services tailored to the needs of crisis-affected youth. By prioritizing inclusivity and educational access, NRC seeks to promote positive learning outcomes and reduce dropout rates.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtNRC’s participatory, community-centered approach ensures that all interventions are developed in collaboration with local stakeholders and tailored to meet the specific needs of each community. By leveraging local capacities, fostering social cohesion, and enhancing resilience, NRC aims to deliver immediate lifesaving assistance while laying the groundwork for sustainable recovery and durable solutions. This intervention aligns with the objectives of the 2024 Third Reserve Allocation Strategy by addressing critical humanitarian needs and supporting recovery and resilience-building efforts in Ethiopia’s contested areas. ltbrgtlt/pgt
